newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude firm on technicals, heat up on gas oil.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude firm on technicals, heat up on gas oil.

text.p: NYMEX crude remained firm Monday afternoon after holding trendline support during earlier profit-taking, while a gas oil futures rally in London boosted heating oil, traders said.
"Crude held support while heating oil has fallen below it's 20-day (simple) moving average. But, as long as gas oil is strong, heat's not going to give," said a dealer.

At 1327 EST, February crude was up 16 cents at $25.38 a barrel. Feb crude hit a contract high of $25.55 at the open and then fell to a session low of $25.12, holding trendline support extending from the December 11 low of $23.15.
January heating oil was up 0.40 cent a gallon at 70.95 cents. On London's IPE, January gas oil settled up $6.00 a tonne at $223.00 amid artic temperatures sweeping Europe.

January gasoline was off 0.24 cent at 69.50 cents a gallon on weakness in the gasoline-to-crude crack spread, traders said. Upside in the refined product prompt months was limited by the expiry in the January contract Tuesday.
Prices were rangebound in thin volume ahead of the New Year's holiday Wednesday, priming the oil complex for a technical breakout after the holiday this week or early next week, traders said.
"The range is tightening into a coil, and eventually, it's going to break out on either side," said a dealer.
Noting the bearish above-average temperature forecasts for the key heating oil market of the northeastern United States near term, dealers thought a decline in heat was likely.
Support for Feb crude was pegged at around $25.10 and $25.00, while minor support for Feb heating oil, the front month after Tuesday, was pegged at around 69.80 cents.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
